name: Meowdulator
description: The Meowdulator is a very silly pedal that makes cat noises. It only carries a single octave worth of meows, so it is very limited for use with chords. All the knobs are labeled 'Meow'. There are a few different cat voices to choose from. This pedal is a special co-promotion with B's Music, so it has the B's Music logo (on the microphone).

name: Atreides
description: The name comes from the 'weirding module' invented for David Lynch's Dune, and it is that strange. Kind of a fuzz, but also kind of a synthesizer, it's more of a toy than a tone shaper.

name: Bass Synth
description: If you need that synthesizer bass sound from your bass, this will do it. Better at handling low end frequencies than other synth pedals.

name: NS-2 Noise Suppressor
description: Does exactly what the name says. Most effective when noisy pedals are contained in a four-cable send and return loop. But can also go anywhere in the chain and filter other kinds of noise.

name: Cry Baby
description: The classic, base-model wah. No frills, all analog.

name: Ditto X2
description: The Ditto is a full-featured looping pedal. You can slow down or reverse the loop, but my favorite feature is the easy stop. The stereo output at the end of the chain is also incredibly handy.

name: Fuzz Factory
description: Five controls for a fuzz pedal is a lot, and this one is capable of dialing in a ton of custom sounds. When I got it used, some of the original black knobs were damaged, so I replaced all of them with multi-colored knobs. It seemed to fit the pedal.

name: Garbage Face
description: This fuzz is a collaboration between the manufacturer and J Mascis, the guitarist from Dinosaur Jr. There are two separate volume controls for the fuzz, and you can switch between them. In true J Mascis style, there's also a treble boost that you can tap for a little extra power.

name: Ghost Writer
description: The Ghost Writer is a simple transformer that allows you to use a guitar as a MIDI controller. This allows you to plug it into a synthesizer or other MIDI device. Comes with a special cable just for this purpose.

name: Iridium
description: Iridium is an amp-in-a-box pedal that lets you dial in a custom amplifier and cabinet profile. It has a headphone jack, so you can use it to play without an actual amplifier.

name: Melon Cube
description: This fuzz has a lot of options for shaping its sound. More friendly sounding than some of the darker muff-style fuzzes out there.

name: Pulp 'N' Peel
description: This compressor will squeeze fresh orange juice out of your guitar. There's also a hidden rat-type distortion circuit that can be activated using bonus controls. This pedal has a huge number of features for its size.

name: Spring King
description: Back in the 60s, surf guitar players would kick their reverb tanks to make the springs inside make a really cool crashing sound. Most modern reverb pedals don't have real springs in them, so it's harder to make that sound. Enter the Spring King: a simple spring reverb that has real springs, and a special kick plate that you can tap with your foot to recreate the sound.

name: Acapulco Gold
description: This powerful distortion, with just one massive level knob, can be dangerous to animals and small children. One of the loudest pedals I've ever used.

name: BD-2 Blues Driver
description: Not sure why they call it a 'Blues' driver, but this overdrive is very versatile and has become quite popular with alternative rock and shoegaze guitarists.

name: Volume Pedal
description: This analog pedal is pretty simple. The foot switch rocks back and forth, with full volume at one end, and mute at the other. Essential for fades and swells.

name: MF-4
description: Fuzzlord makes just one kind of pedal: fuzz. This one has a really grimey and doomy sound, and it cleans up nicely with a distortion nearby. Artwork is... controversial.

name: Green Screamer
description: Every pedal company has their own version of the Ibanez Tube Screamer circuit, and they often make the pedal green to let you know exactly what to expect. I like this one better than most.

name: HM-2w Heavy Metal
description: The original HM-2 was very popular in Nordic countries for some reason, and became the foundation of the Swedish death metal and Norwegian black metal scenes. There's just one way to use this pedal - turn everything up to maximum.

name: Hizumitas
description: A lot of heavy fuzz for such a small pedal with a cute graphic. Apparently based on a custom circuit from a Japanese doom metal artist. Pairs nicely with Plumes.

name: Katzenkönig
description: The name is German for 'cat king', an appropriate name for a ToneBender-style fuzz crossed with a Rat distortion. I like this one because it is lighter than the usual muff-style fuzzes.

name: Kompressor
description: There are a lot of compressors out there, but this one has a lot of knobs. And it's black and looks like metal, which is probably why it has become popular with metal guitarists.

name: Lillian
description: Walrus makes a whole line of tone-shaping effects named after women. There's probably a whole story of who Lillian is. Regardless, this is a very robust phaser.

name: MT-2w Metal Zone
description: The Metal Zone gets a lot of hate for having a thin and shrill sound, but there's a lot more going on here. Name another pedal with four tone controls! If you need to make a Telecaster and a keyboard amp sound like metal, this will do it. And even if you have all your distortion needs managed, this pedal can still be used as an instant feedback circuit.

name: Muffuletta
description: JHS likes to give you a lot of bang for your buck, and this pedal is no exception. If you can't figure out which style of Big Muff you want to buy, they've got you covered. The lower right knob allows you to switch between six different Big Muff sounds, including Pi, Russian, Ram's Head, and more. Named after a delicious deli sandwich that is popular in New Orleans.

name: OS-2 Overdrive Distortion
description: This is a great pedal for beginners. It's capable of a lot of different rock sounds, right out of the box, regardless of your amp or guitar. Pairs well with other distortions. One of the oldest pedals in my collection.

name: Plumes
description: Plumes is my absolute favorite overdrive pedal. It's similar to a Tube Screamer topology, but it's capable of so much more. Pairs nicely with Hizumitas. This is a limited edition color called 'water blue'.

name: Sabbra Cadabra
description: Tony Iommi from Black Sabbath had an instantly recognizable sound, created by his custom Laney amps. If you want that sound, but can't find or afford a vintage amp, this pedal reproduces it like magic.

name: Spark
description: This mini pedal does just one thing, and does it well: boosts your volume. Use it after a volume sucking pedal, or as a boost going into another pedal. Either way, you're guaranteed to be louder.

name: Star Crash
description: This is a Fuzz Face circuit, but with a little bit more volume and some nifty shaping options. Sounds just like the 70s.

name: SY-1 Synthesizer
description: If you want your guitar to go beep-boop, start here. The Boss has eight different sound types, with ten variations of each, which lets you create dozens of sounds. And it has send/return and expression jacks for even more versatility.

name: Sentry
description: The Sentry locks down your sound with the best noise gate on the market. Most effective when noisy pedals are contained in a four-cable send and return loop. Absolutely essential if you have noisy fuzzes and loud distortions in your chain.

name: TU-3w Tuner
description: Boss has been the leader in pedal tuners for decades. And this one's black! I like it because it's responsive enough to reliably tune basses and downtuned guitars.

name: Blood Moon
description: A solid phaser option from TC Electronics' lower tier line.

name: Dark Light
description: OBNE combined their Dark Star lo-fi reverb and their Sunlight dynamic reverb into one crazy pedal that allows you to run them both in parallel or in series. And each side has independent stereo outputs for maximum customization.

name: JVM
description: The JVM is a 100w Marshall all-valve head with an iconic crunch sound that is popular with metal bands. This pedal simulates that distortion sound. It also has a built-in noise gate.

name: Notaklön
description: One of the most unique pedal concepts ever conceived. The Klon is a an extremely rare and highly coveted overdrive pedal that is famously hard to emulate because the original developer covered the electronics in a substance called goop, so no one could reverse engineer it. Those who have played a Klon claim that it is pure magic. So when JHS was able to reverse engineer the sound of the original, they wanted to do something clever with it. The Notaklön is a spoof on an IKEA furniture item, and it comes as a kit that you have to assemble yourself. It even includes a tube of goop that you can apply to the circuit board. To be perfectly honest, I don't think the Klon is all that special, and although this version of it sounds accurate, I'm not a huge fan. But it was all worth it to have a pedal that I assembled myself in my collection. (I did not apply the goop.)

name: Psi
description: The Psi has a similar fuzz sound to the Big Muff Pi, but it's not as thick sounding, which is why this was my first fuzz pedal.

name: TS-9 Tube Screamer
description: Iconic sound and iconic color - every company has a Tube Screamer clone, and they're all the exact same shade of green.

name: Grunge
description: DOD was a popular effects brand in the 80s, but when they started losing market share to Boss, they kinda lost their minds trying to come up with new ways to market themselves in the 90s. The Grunge comes from this era, although the name is more closely related to the grunge aesthetic than any of the original Seattle sounds of the genre. It is both a fuzz and a distortion, and while it excels at neither, it is capable of making a lot of noise.

name: Chug
description: When you let a Swedish death metal player design a distortion pedal for serious riffing, this is the result. The end goal is to have a distortion unit that can turn any combination of amp and guitar into a metal monster. There are so many different controls on this pedal, and you will probably have to have help to find a configuration for your particular setup. But you can't argue with the end result - pure metal madness.

name: Black Fountain
description: Black Fountain is a stereo oil-can delay which has different timers for each channel. Lots of configuration options, it can go from simple delay to something approaching noise.

name: DD-8 Digital Delay
description: The Swiss Army knife of digital delays. It has multiple different modes, to emulate multiple different delay sounds.

name: Dookie
description: Billie Joe Armstrong used a couple modified Marshall amps to record the guitar sounds on Green Day's album 'Dookie'. The two amp heads were wired together, and could be blended between overdrive and distortion. This pedal emulates that sound, and the blend knob works the same way. There's also a finger-switch that scoops the mids.

name: Dual Wreck
description: One of the most famous metal sounds of the 90s came from the Mesa Boogie Dual Rectifier amp. This pedal is an affordable way to get that sound.

name: EM-III
description: This echo pedal simulates a magnetic tape delay effect, with controls for flutter and color. If you hold the tap tempo switch, it can really warp the delay sound.

name: Flight Delay
description: Is it digital? Is it analog? Is it a reverse delay? Yes. There's so many switches and knobs on this thing, you'll go crazy. Another example of a JHS pedal for the perpetually undecided.

name: Less Than Jake
description: Less Than Jake is a ska-punk band, and their songs often switch between a boosted clean sound and a thick distortion. Naturally, this pedal does the same. The ska side has just one knob, for boost level. And the punk side is a fully configurable distortion.

name: Lore
description: Lore is a dedicated reverse reverb unit. Reverse reverb has a digital buffer, so the reverb sounds like it happens before the notes you play. The more you crank it, the more confusing it sounds, but it's an essential shoegaze effect.

name: Mandala
description: Mandala has eight different glitch effects with various timing mechanisms, to make it sound like you're losing control of your electronics. Can sound like anything from a Matrix-style digital clipping to a bad cable.

name: MT-2 Metal Zone
description: The Metal Zone gets a lot of hate for having a thin and shrill sound, but there's a lot more going on here. Name another pedal with four tone controls! If you need to make a Telecaster and a keyboard amp sound like metal, this will do it. And even if you have all your distortion needs managed, this pedal can still be used as an instant feedback circuit. This one is pretty old, and has seen much better days.

name: Morning Glory
description: A lot of overdrives feel pretty similar, but this one has a unique feature. The blend knob allows you to mix your clean signal with the overdriven one, creating a subtle array of tones.

name: RV-6 Reverb
description: The Swiss Army knife of digital reverbs. It has multiple different modes, to emulate multiple different reverb sounds.

name: Screen Violence
description: A collaboration with the synth-pop group Chvrches. The 'violence' channel is a simple overdrive circuit. And the screen channel has multiple modes of modulation effects.

name: Shermy
description: Collaboration with Miss Shermette of The Surfrajettes. It's Solid Gold's Surf Rider spring reverb, but in a more compact form factor, and with a more retro color.

name: AC-3 Acoustic Simulator
description: Sometimes, you really need your electric guitar to sound like an acoustic guitar. I don't think this pedal does a very good job of that, but it does add some interesting color to your electric guitar sound. Just get an acoustic guitar if you need one. If you go to Mexico, they're cheaper than this pedal.

name: Afterneath
description: The graphic of a wizard in a cave casting spells pretty much says it all. It starts off as a room reverb, but then you have massive control over what happens to the reflections. Popular with dream pop and shoegaze bands.

name: Alpha Haunt
description: And out come the wolves! Sure it's a fuzz, but OBNE never stops there. You also get a three-band equalizer, and plenty of tweaking knobs and switches.

name: Angry Charlie
description: Angry Charlie is a simulator of the JCM-800 Marshall amp, and has all the overdrive and distortion capabilities of that classic head.

name: Arrow Airwaves
description: This is one of the most unique pedals I own - I've never seen anyone else with this on their board. Maybe for good reason. It generates static. There are three different modes: it can play only static all the time, it can play static while you play, or it can play static when you stop playing. Very limited lo-fi applications, but it is absolutely perfect when you actually want static.

name: Attack Decay
description: This pedal is a type of delay called a tape reverse simulator. It's based on what it sound like if you play a reel-to-reel tape machine in reverse. Basically, it makes your music backwards.

name: Bit Commander
description: Bit Commander is a bit crusher - it compresses your sound so hard that it becomes pixelated. This is not quite the same as making classic 8-bit video game music, so you can't really use it to make chiptunes. But if you really want to squelch and squeeze your sound, this will do it.

name: CH-1 Super Chorus
description: This is the gold standard of chorus pedals - so much so that other manufacturers make their chorus pedals the same color.

name: DS-1 Distortion
description: This basic, beginner-level distortion became famous when it was revealed that Kurt Cobain used it on the Nirvana album 'Bleach'.

name: Ledges
description: Ledges does three different types of reverb - hall, room, and plate. I got this because I didn't actually own any other plate reverb pedals.

name: Mimiq
description: Mimiq is a very specialized application of a chorus circuit. It emulates the multi-tracked guitar sounds you sometimes hear on albums, when the same guitar tracks are layered on top of each other to fatten up the sound. It's not really useful for live situations, but if you want to get as close to a recorded sound as possible, this can help.

name: Six Band EQ
description: As with most equalizers, vertical center is flat, up is boosted, and down is diminished. The classic V-shape shown here is called 'scooped mids' - the midrange frequencies are turned way down.

name: OC-5 Octave
description: This pedal can create three octaves - one up, two up, and one down. There are enough controls to play all three at once if you want. This pedal has a switch on the back that lets you switch between the bass or guitar.

name: FX40 Soft Focus
description: This pedal is based on the circuit of a particular rack-mount multi-effects unit that created a special reverb sound that was the center of Slowdive's shoegaze sound on their album 'Souvlaki'. The graphic evokes the LCD display of the original unit.

name: Soul Vibe
description: Not actually a tremolo, but a rotovibe. The rotovibe was a kind of speaker that rotated, which created a uniquely dopplered tremolo effect. As the name of this pedal might suggest, it was a common sound in 60s funk, and Jimi Hendrix was a fan of the sound.

name: Topanga
description: Topanga is one of the best spring reverbs I have ever played. Amazing replica of the Fender spring tank.

name: AD-2 Acoustic Preamp
description: Not all amplifiers have preamps specifically designed for acoustic guitars, so here comes Boss to the rescue. Even if it is an acoustic amp, you might want this pedal.

name: Aqueduct
description: The Aqueduct is a vibrato pedal, which modulates the pitch of the frequency. This pedal has eight different pitch shifting algorithms to choose from. Like many Earthquaker pedals, this one has a non-latching switch, so you can temporarily engage the effect with a half-press.

name: Aural Destiny
description: This pedal is a cornucopia of atmospheric reverbs. The shimmer mode sounds unbelievable when paired with a 12-string guitar.

name: Avalanche Run
description: With a reverb and a delay in the same stereo pedal, this unit is almost shoegaze-in-a-box. The reverb is similar to the Afterneath, although with fewer knobs.

name: Bass Big Muff π
description: You can use a normal Big Muff with a bass - they're plenty bassy on their own. But this one is specifically designed for lower frequencies.

name: Bass Octave Deluxe
description: Gotta love the labels on these knobs. If you need octaves on your bass, get them here.

name: Blumes
description: Blumes is basically a Plumes overdrive, but designed for the bass. You might not think you need one, until you hear it.

name: Cloudburst
description: This pedal is the master of atmospheric reverb. With the mix and decay turned all the way up, it will ring for days.

name: Clover
description: This pedal only exists to make everything sound bigger and better. Between the clean boost and the tone controls, what's not to love?

name: EQ-200
description: Sometimes, six bands of EQ just isn't enough. Which is why this one has ten. Plus a level set, which effectively makes this a boost pedal.

name: Hello Kitty Fuzz
description: To be perfectly honest, I bought this as a gag, because I didn't own any pink pedals. But it's an amazing light-sounding fuzz.

name: Hummingbird
description: This aptly named pedal has the angry energy of a tiny bird rapidly flapping its wings. Like many Earthquaker pedals, this one has a non-latching switch, so you can temporarily engage the effect with a half-press.

name: Tinytuner
description: This mini tuner is dirt cheap and works great for electric guitar and bass. However, it struggles with acoustics and my 7-string guitar.

name: Expression Ramper
description: Many pedals have what is called an expression input, which allows you to control the application of the effect with an external rocker switch (similar to a wah or volume pedal). A ramper plugs into that same input, and allows you to bring the effect up or down with a simple tap.

name: Acoustic Preverb
description: This pedal combines an acoustic preamp and an acoustic reverb in a shiny copper case.

name: Sea Machine
description: Sea Machine begins as a simple chorus, but it has the ability to quickly go rogue. At a certain point, all you can hear is bubbles under the water. Like many Earthquaker pedals, this one has a non-latching switch, so you can temporarily engage the effect with a half-press.

name: Slapback Echo
description: A sound wave that hits the wall very quickly and bounces back with very little degradation is called a slapback echo. Think of the sound you hear on a racquetball court. This delay only makes that one sound, with minimal controls.

name: Soul Preacher
description: It says 'compressor/sustainer' right there on the pedal, and that's what it does. The compression is simple, but the sustain is massive.

name: Spatial Delivery
description: It's hard to describe exactly what this pedal does, but the best thing to say is that it warps the sound. This is pedal you should only use if you need some weirdness.

name: Surfybear Reverb
description: This pedal is extremely long because it has real springs inside, which give it outstanding spring reverb sound. There are two channels, so you can switch between levels of reverb mix. I recommend not setting this on the floor in front of your amp, because the vibrations from the speaker will actually rattle the springs and create extra reverb.

name: Vortex
description: Entry-level flanger. If you only have a few bucks to spend, and you need to play the opening from the Heart song 'Barracuda', start here.

name: Thunderstorm
description: Thanks to cheap overseas assembly, this pedal actually cost less than my mini Vortex flanger, even though it is all-analog circuitry.

name: TU-3 Tuner
description: No frills tuner, handles all my instruments perfectly.

name: Tremolo
description: I don't think there's a better, warmer sounding tremolo out there. Voodoo Labs doesn't make many pedals, but the ones they do make are excellent.

name: Whitecap
description: Tremolo is a fun effect, but what if you made it unfun? This pedal lets you set two tremolos, with independent rates, at the same time - either in parallel or in series. I haven't found a setting on this pedal that is harmonious.
